# Accepted dependency advisories for the pip-audit gate in .github/workflows/ci.yml
#
# Format: one advisory ID per line. Everything after `#` is a comment.
#
# RULES:
#   1. Every entry needs a reason and a review date. No bare IDs.
#   2. An entry is a decision to SHIP a known vulnerability. It is not a way to
#      make CI green - if you cannot write a defensible reason, fix the dependency.
#   3. Re-check every entry at its review date. Suppressions rot: a CVE with no
#      fix today usually has one in three months.
#
# To suppress nothing, leave this file with comments only - that is the goal state.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CURRENT STATUS: nothing suppressed.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# `pip-audit` on the current lockfile reports 16 advisories across 3 packages:
#
#   starlette         0.46.2   9 advisories  (fixes exist: 0.47.2 -> 1.3.1)
#   python-multipart  0.0.20   6 advisories  (fixes exist: 0.0.22 -> 0.0.31)
#   ecdsa             0.19.2   1 advisory    (PYSEC-2026-1325, NO fix available)
#
# These are deliberately NOT suppressed here. They are real, they are fixable
# (except ecdsa), and suppressing them on day one would make this gate
# decorative. The dependency bumps are a separate, reviewable change:
#
#   - starlette/python-multipart come in transitively via fastapi. Upgrading
#     means moving fastapi forward and re-running the full suite; starlette 1.x
#     is a major version and is NOT a drop-in for fastapi 0.115.
#   - ecdsa comes in via python-jose. It has no fix available, so the real
#     remediation is migrating off python-jose (PyJWT is the usual replacement),
#     not a version bump.
#
# Until that change lands, this job WILL fail. That is the correct signal - see
# docs/deployment/DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md ("Known security debt") for the triage
# decision and the two options for unblocking.
